cards.card: 三菱ＵＦＪカード ゴールド
三菱ＵＦＪカード・プラチナ・アメリカン・エキスプレス・カード
JCB カード W plus L
エポスゴールドカード

note: Japan's three largest banking groups issue their credit cards through their card companies: MUFG through Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS, SMBC through Sumitomo Mitsui Card, and Mizuho through its card partners. Sumitomo Mitsui Card's and Mizuho Bank's sites refuse this research's requests (Akamai, 'Access Denied', 2026-10-30), so JCB, the country's own card brand and one of its largest issuers, is written in their place. Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS's pages, as of 28 September 2026, read 2026-10-30: the MUFG Card (三菱ＵＦＪカード) has no annual fee, ever; the MUFG Card Gold costs 11,000 yen a year including tax, its first-year waiver being for those who join on the web, a condition the game doesn't check, so the fee is written in full; the MUFG Card Platinum American Express costs 22,000 yen a year. Revolving (its registered revolving service, 楽Ｐａｙ) carries 19.80% a year (実質年率, charged by the day on the balance carried, written as a yearly rate), which replaces the 18.00% this file held from 2026-10-29; the page says a few cards differ, without naming them, and 19.80% is written on all three. A cash advance (キャッシングサービス) carries 17.95% a year (融資利率, 実質年率). The annual-fee reduction for revolving users, the ETC and UnionPay cards' issue fees, the statement-by-post fee and the late charge (遅延損害金, set in the member agreement as the statutory rate, read but not written, the game having no statutory rate) aren't written; nor is a foreign-transaction fee, the member agreement (個人会員規約, read 2026-10-30) adding only 'a fee the company sets' to the exchange rate without a figure. JCB's pages (as of August 2026, read 2026-10-30): the JCB Card W and W plus L (open to those 18 to 39 when they apply, an age the game doesn't check at application) and the JCB Card S have no annual fee; JCB Gold costs 11,000 yen a year including tax, its first year free; JCB Platinum 27,500 yen. Revolving carries 18.00% a year (実質年率), to which JCB moved its cards from 1 October 2026 (some cards may differ, the page says). JCB's cash advance rate, minimum payment and foreign-transaction fee weren't found on the pages read and aren't written. Japanese cards are paid in full each month by default (monthly closing on the 15th, payment on the 10th of the next month), revolving only where the holder chooses it; no grace period in the game's sense is stated. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Epos Card (エポスカード, the Marui group's card company, one of the large card issuers whose rates and fees are on its own pages) is added as a third issuer, Sumitomo Mitsui Card and Mizuho's sites still refusing this research and AEON Card's answering 403 (2026-10-30; Rakuten Card's didn't answer). Epos Card's pages (read 2026-10-30): the Epos Card has no joining or annual fee, ever; the Epos Gold Card's annual fee is normally 5,000 yen, and a year with 500,000 yen or more spent makes it free from the next year on for good (written as a yearly fee waived by 500,000 yen spent in the year); shopping revolving (ショッピングリボ払い) carries 18.0% a year (実質年率), and a cash advance (キャッシング) 18.0% a year. The Epos Platinum Card's page didn't give its fee to this research and isn't written; no foreign-transaction fee, minimum payment or late charge figure was on the pages read. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: A Japanese card's statement asks the whole balance unless the holder has registered for revolving, whose rate each card here carries; its least monthly payment is written. MUFG's 楽Pay page (read 2026-10-30): the holder sets the monthly payment anywhere from 3,000 to 100,000 yen, principal and fee together (within) or the fee on top (without); written at the least, 3,000 yen with the fee within, as a floor on a 0% share. No minimum in the form is published for JCB's cards: its revolving page (read 2026-10-30) sets the principal by a course chosen, the least (ゆとりコース) 5,000 yen up to a balance of 100,000, 10,000 to 500,000, 15,000 to 1,000,000 and 20,000 above, plus the fee, a step by balance the form doesn't hold, and its fixed course names no least sum. No minimum payment is published for Epos Card's two cards; tried: its revolving and course-change pages (no figures), a web search, and archive.org (no answer).
